title: Start a business, not a startup
coreMove: A startup is still a business: it must earn more than it spends. Make the path to a paying customer visible from day one, even if first amounts stay modest.

exampleSpecs.audience: founders choosing how the venture gets funded
exampleSpecs.stakes: build on customer payment or on investor capital
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist picks customer-funded over investor-funded software

exampleSpecs.audience: teams running on a raise with no paid users
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep spending capital or test whether anyone will pay
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist sees investor money hiding the willingness-to-pay test

exampleSpecs.stakes: treat later as a schedule or as a missing answer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist exposes deferred profit as a masked unproven model

exampleSpecs.audience: builders deciding when profit pressure starts
exampleSpecs.stakes: treat profit as early constraint or late cleanup
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: profit pressure sharpens value, support, pricing, and restraint

exampleSpecs.audience: founders confusing the edge with instant riches
exampleSpecs.stakes: demand instant large profit or a visible path
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist applies the edge as a visible path, not instant profit

exampleSpecs.audience: founders who think business sounds small-minded
exampleSpecs.stakes: chase startup mythology or build an ambitious business
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist reframes business as clarifying, not limiting
